name: Turing Machine 2D
miniText: How can small read-write agents perform complicated computation on a shared field? NetLogo Turing Machine 2D extends the tape idea to a two-dimensional patch array and potentially many heads. Each head follows a transition table determined by its internal state and the current patch value, changing state, writing, and choosing a movement direction. Turing [1] provides the foundational computational formalism; Langton's self-reproduction study [2] and artificial-life work [3] connect local machines with spatial construction and collective patterns. The NetLogo baseline is a finite multihead teaching variant, not Turing's original one-dimensional tape. Shared writes and head activation order can affect interactions. An intricate picture does not prove universal computation or successful parallelism. The simulation illustrates explicit state transitions and the consequences of allowing several processors to modify one environment.
